# HTTPRetry 0.9

HTTPRetry is a lightweight Python library that retries failed HTTP requests, so network hiccups, rate limits, and flaky APIs don't crash your app.

Version 0.9 uses exponential backoff, so the wait between retries grows and you stop hammering a server that's already struggling. It also adds jitter, a random offset to each delay, so clients that failed together don't all retry at the same moment and swamp the service again (the "thundering herd" problem).

The library has no dependencies, so there's nothing extra to install and nothing to conflict with your other packages. Test coverage is at 94%.

It works for microservices, scrapers, and third-party API integrations. Install it, wrap your requests, and transient failures get retried instead of turning into errors.
